name: Jay Blue
lede: Jay Blue is a moderate, slightly greyed blue named for the jay bird, and it most often plays an accent color inside a painting.

sections.title: A bird's name
sections.body:
The library records Jay Blue from the 1912 Ridgway atlas, plate XXII, hue 47, tone i, carried into the ISCC-NBS system's block 182 in 1955 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[azure-blue]], [[chapman-s-blue]], [[stardew]] and [[indigo-blue]], at 2.6, 2.6, 
In LCH terms it measures lightness 46, chroma 24, hue 274 degrees, the ISCC-NBS "moderate blue" block, Munsell 5.2PB 4.5/5.6, close to [[azure-blue|Azure Blue]] and [[steel-blue|Steel Blue]] [1]. 6, 2.6, 3.7 and 3.8 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in 175 of 23,781 paintings, 0.74 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 83 [2]. That makes it more common than 56 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 20 of 1,674 paintings, at 1.2 percent of that century's paintings, 2.5 times the expected rate, and it is over-represented in French paintings, 2.3 times expected, 29 of 3,443 [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as an accent, in 48 percent of its appearances [2].

The earliest match is dated 1420, by Fra Angelico; that is 492 years before the name's own first record, in 1912, so the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not evidence of the actual paint, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].

origin.named_after: pairs the jay bird with blue; the library does not say which jay species, if any, it intends
